name: Responsible Disclosure Policy
metaDescription: Review the rules for reporting suspected security vulnerabilities affecting approved Cybersentinels-owned public systems.

blocks.text: [FULL LEGAL ENTITY NAME], trading as Cybersentinels Consulting, values good-faith reports that help us identify and address security issues in approved Cybersentinels-owned public systems. This policy explains the limited testing we authorize, how to report a suspected vulnerability and the conduct required for coordinated disclosure.
This is not a bug-bounty program and does not promise payment, reward, recognition or employment.
Only the exact assets listed below are in scope:

items: [EXACT PRODUCTION DOMAIN OR SUBDOMAIN]
[EXACT PUBLIC APPLICATION OR API]
[OTHER SPECIFIC ASSET OR REMOVE]

blocks.text: If an asset is not expressly listed, it is out of scope. Client systems, partner systems, employee accounts, third-party services, social accounts, infrastructure not owned by Cybersentinels and lookalike domains are out of scope even if they reference Cybersentinels.

items: Comply with applicable law and this policy
Use only accounts and data you own or are expressly authorized to use
Use the minimum testing necessary to confirm a suspected issue
Stop immediately if you encounter personal, confidential, client or third-party information
Do not access, copy, alter, retain, download, transmit or disclose data beyond the minimum unavoidable observation
Do not establish persistence, pivot, escalate privileges beyond minimum confirmation or attempt lateral movement
Do not disrupt availability, performance, monitoring, logging or another user
Do not publicly disclose the issue before written coordination with us
Report promptly using the approved channel and provide accurate, reproducible information
Delete any inadvertently retained information after we confirm receipt and when legally permitted
Denial-of-service, resource exhaustion, stress or load testing
Social engineering, phishing, impersonation or physical intrusion
Malware, ransomware, destructive payloads, persistence or command-and-control
Password spraying, credential stuffing, brute force or use of leaked credentials
Testing involving employees, clients, partners or other users
Accessing messages, files, databases, secrets or personal information
Changing, deleting, corrupting, encrypting or exfiltrating data
Automated scanning at a volume that could affect service or create excessive alerts
Testing third-party services, dependencies or infrastructure without their separate authorization
Extortion, threats, demands or conditioning non-disclosure on payment
Public disclosure before remediation coordination
Any activity prohibited by law or outside the listed scope

blocks.text: Send reports to [MONITORED SECURITY EMAIL ADDRESS]. For sensitive reports, use [PGP PUBLIC KEY LINK AND FINGERPRINT OR APPROVED SECURE SUBMISSION PORTAL]. Do not use the general contact or careers form.

items: Affected in-scope asset and exact location
Description and potential impact
Clear reproduction steps
Minimal proof such as sanitized request and response details
Date, time and relevant test account
Tools and IP addresses used, if helpful for log review
Whether any data or another user may have been affected
Your preferred contact details and disclosure expectations

blocks.text: Do not attach unnecessary personal information, client data, credentials, secrets, executable malware or large data extracts.
We will make reasonable efforts to:

items: Acknowledge a valid channel report within [TARGET BUSINESS DAYS]
Review whether the report affects an in-scope Cybersentinels-owned asset
Request clarification where needed
Provide periodic updates when practical
Coordinate remediation and any agreed disclosure

blocks.text: Targets are not service-level commitments. Response and remediation time depend on severity, reproducibility, complexity, dependencies and risk. We may not provide technical detail about internal remediation or third-party systems.

If you make a good-faith effort to comply with this policy, stay within the listed scope and avoid harm, we will not initiate legal action against you solely for that authorized research. If a third party initiates action and you complied with this policy, we may clarify that your activity was conducted under this policy where appropriate and legally permitted.

This statement does not bind third parties, regulators or law-enforcement authorities; excuse unlawful conduct; authorize activity on systems we do not own; waive rights relating to extortion, threats, data misuse or harm; or prevent action required to protect users, clients or systems. If you are uncertain whether an action is permitted, stop and ask us before proceeding.

Do not publicly disclose a suspected or confirmed issue, related technical detail or affected information until we provide written approval or the parties agree on a coordinated disclosure date. We will consider reasonable disclosure requests but must protect users, clients, systems and legal obligations.

We do not currently operate a monetary bug-bounty program. Any recognition or reward is entirely discretionary, subject to eligibility, law, sanctions, tax, identity and other checks, and must be confirmed in writing. Do not conduct testing with an expectation of payment.

We use reporter contact and report information to investigate, communicate, protect systems, maintain records, comply with law and establish or defend legal claims. See the Privacy Notice for additional information. Avoid submitting unnecessary personal information.
We may update, suspend or withdraw this policy. Testing is governed by the version in effect when the activity occurs. Check this page before testing.
Policy questions: [SECURITY OR LEGAL EMAIL ADDRESS]

items: Replace all square-bracketed contact and legal placeholders.
Confirm the founding year, headquarters wording and the 20+ client statement.
Obtain written approval before displaying any client name, logo, testimonial or identifiable case study.
Confirm that every listed service is currently deliverable directly or through an approved delivery model.
Validate regulatory and standards-related wording before publication and whenever applicable requirements change.
Do not describe SOC 2 as a certification or imply that Cybersentinels issues certifications, attestations or formal assessment outcomes.
Do not use certification or accreditation logos without documented authorization.
Connect every CTA to the relevant page, form or scheduling workflow.
Test inquiry and newsletter consent flows against the final Privacy Notice.
Review the final website copy after design implementation to ensure that headings, qualifiers and disclaimers have not been removed or separated from their context.
